title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Client Whereabouts Unknown
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal's client completely stops returning calls or emails for six months. A crucial tribunal filing deadline is approaching. The paralegal has exhausted all avenues to locate the client and decides they must withdraw. How should the paralegal proceed?
options: Simply close the file and move on; no notice is required if the client is missing.
Withdraw silently but file a claim against the client for abandoned file fees.
Document all reasonable attempts to locate the client, notify the tribunal of the withdrawal if required by tribunal rules, and protect the client's file.
Draft a fictitious affidavit claiming the client is dead to secure an adjournment.
questions.explain: When a client disappears, the paralegal cannot simply abandon the file without creating a paper trail. They must take all reasonable steps to locate/notify the client (documented), seek leave to withdraw from the tribunal if there is an active proceeding, and safeguard the client's documents in case they return.
